Apple has initiated strategic partnerships with several major healthcare systems to integrate its Health platform into clinical workflows, positioning the company to tap into the growing digital health market and diversify revenue beyond traditional hardware sales, potentially contributing to a 5% price increase.
2. A growth slowdown and margin compression combine to a 5% stock price decrease. iPhone shipments fell 12% YoY, reducing revenue growth to 4% from 7%, and gross margin fell 150 bps to 31.5%. Operating leverage translates to a 6% EPS miss versus consensus, which our valuation model estimates to be a 5% stock price decrease.
3. Internal reports from a key component supplier for the upcoming Vision Pro 2 indicate significant manufacturing yield issues with the new generation of micro-OLED displays. This challenge is expected to delay the product's launch by at least six months, impacting future revenue diversification narratives and potentially causing a modest stock price decline of 5%.
4. Company operating margin rose 1.2 percentage points to 29.8% year over year, revenue grew 3.9% year over year, and share count declined 1.0%; combined, these factors lift expected EPS by 5.1% relative to the consensus for the next 12 months. Assuming a static price-to-earnings ratio of 27.5 at the time of the shift, the EPS boost implies a price increase of 5.1%.
